problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{1}{6}$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ rounded to $1$ decimal place?
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{1}{6})=-0.167\,448…≈-0.167\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-0.167$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-0.167\,4.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.167\,4.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.167\,4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/dc7d405cfe1d3f36b0132fe32cd3e74056dd6cc6f33b0fdd786cc870eb24c1da.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +0.167\,4 \\  & ≈3.309\,0\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we simply subtract $2\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=X-2\pi  & ≈3.309-2\pi ≈-2.974\,2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=(-0.167\,4)\cdot (-2.974\,2)≈0.5,
$$

rounded to $1$ decimal place.
